title: Color Codes
body:
Syntax: prompt <text with &&codes>  |  description <text with &&codes>  |  biography <text with &&codes>

Description: Color codes add color to text you write yourself -- your prompt ('prompt'), description ('description'), and biography ('biography') all support them.

A code is an && followed by one letter, applying to everything after it until the next code or a reset. Always end colored text with &&x to reset back to normal.

Standard colors:
  &&R red      &&G green    &&Y yellow   &&B blue
  &&C cyan     &&M magenta  &&W white    &&D dark gray

Bright/bold versions -- same letters, lowercase:
  &&r bright red      &&g bright green    &&y bright yellow   &&b bright blue
  &&c bright cyan     &&m bright magenta  &&w bright white    &&d bright gray

Two more:
  &&O orange (a convenience shortcut -- see below for how it's made)
  &&x reset -- turns color back off; always use this when you're done

256-color codes: &&[N] where N is a number from 0 to 255, for finer shades than the named codes above (&&O orange is actually &&[208] under the hood). Example: &&[196] is a bright red, &&[27] is a deep blue.

Example: prompt &&RHP:%h&&x sets your prompt so 'HP:' shows in red and the rest stays normal.

(If a code ever needs to appear as plain text instead of applying its color -- like every example on this very page -- type &&&& instead of a single &&.)

If you'd rather see plain text with no color at all, ask a staff member -- there's no player-facing toggle for this yet.

Date: 2026-08-17
